title: Conscience-Driven Five-Dimensional Mind Model —— Problem Redefinition and Cognitive Extrapolation in Open Complex Giant Systems
abstract: In the evolution and governance of open complex giant systems, an enduring paradox persists acrossmanagement science and cybernetics: cohorts of elite problem-solvers—possessing stellar credentials,immaculate analytical rigor, and superior intellect—optimize every local key performance indicator(KPI) to perfection under established rules, only to trigger mutual vector cancellation that drives theglobal system into deadlock or catastrophic collapse. Conversely, an exceedingly rare archetype—the“Chief Architect”—possesses the distinct capacity to step outside the game board when establishedrules fail, fundamentally redefining foundational axioms and systemic victory criteria.Departing from Occam’s razor, this treatise presents a unified cognitive architecture bridging micro-neurobiological foundations, macro-cybernetic frameworks, and broad pragmatic explanatory power.We demonstrate that the capacity to “redefine problems” and execute “cognitive extrapolation” undernovel environmental shocks does not stem from mystical inspiration. Rather, it is governed by anirreducible, serially coupled five-dimensional second-order self-healing control loop executed acrossfoundational brain nuclei: Residual Sensitivity (hairs on the skin), Embodied Conscience (brakepads in the heart), Emotional Cache (old scars in the body), Fluid Intelligence (new abacus inhand), and Metacognition (eyes gazing at the sky).This work elucidates the micro-physical mechanisms of the predictive brain across signal cancellation,visceral braking, manifold pruning, causal DAG reconstruction, and meta-language overhaul. Weformalize the Thermodynamic Ignition Law of Conscience and the Non-Compensatory MinimumLaw (Liebig’s Law of the Mind). Furthermore, to overcome the statistical rarity of single-braincomplete profiles (∼ 10−6), we formulate the human-machine orthogonal tensor architecture for QianXuesen’s Department of Overall Design: ΦOrg = ΦHuman ⊗ 𝐴Silicon. Finally, we establish a falsifiableexperimental paradigm based on the “Hidden Rule Mutation Game” and reveal the neuro-architecturalimpossibility of contemporary Large Language Models (LLMs) serving as Chief Architects. Thisresearch establishes an unshakeable theoretical foundation for identifying and safeguarding strategiccognitive assets and engineering carbon-silicon symbiotic architectures in an era of rapid turbulence.

title: Privacy data encryption & deletion while preserving analytical integrity
abstract: Privacy regulations around the world impose strict requirements on how organisations handle personal data (such as the Australian Privacy Act, the EU's GDPR, US's HIPAA & CCPA, etc). Among the hardest to implement in a data pipeline are: protecting sensitive data from breaches, and erasing an individual's personal data on request. Finding and deleting every copy of sensitive data is cumbersome, error-prone, and breaks referential and analytical integrity. Meanwhile, sensitive data sitting in plaintext is exposed the moment a breach occurs. The author proposes practical implementation solutions to integrate the crypto-shredding pattern in analytical data platform's pipeline architecture, enabled by the open-source Python library GDPR-officer created by the author. Sensitive fields are encrypted with a unique encryption key per data subject (e.g. customer), before data is loaded into the platform, restricting access and protecting it during leaks. Analytical sensitive fields are generalised to enable analytics use, while protecting the original value. Encryption keys are stored separately outside the data platform, ensuring sensitive data stays unreadable even when the data platform is breached. Data erasure becomes a single operation: delete the encryption key, and the respective customer's data is rendered permanently unreadable across all tables, without modifying or scanning any data, preserving analytics and referential integrity. Decrypts sensitive data under authorisation for any customer whose key is maintained. The author introduces the architecture, the cryptographic foundations of the Python library, and practical integration into Python ingestion pipelines as well as managed ingestion pipelines. She further proposes a governance framework for encryption key management, rotation, retention, and role-based policies. A live demo of the library is shown during PyCon AU 2026.

title: Can Artificial Intelligence Reach the Women Who Need It? A Scoping Review of Artificial Intelligence for Cervical Cancer Prevention, Screening and Diagnosis in Africa
abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly proposed to address cervical cancer screening and diagnostic gaps in Africa, where shortages of specialist personnel, limited pathology capacity and variable access to screening remain major barriers. Although several AI tools have reported strong algorithmic performance, it is unclear how far they have progressed from development and validation to real-world delivery within African health systems. Existing reviews have largely focused on diagnostic accuracy rather than this translational pathway. This review therefore mapped the extent, nature and implementation maturity of AI applications for cervical cancer prevention, screening and diagnosis in Africa using a Predict–Detect–Reach framework. Methods A scoping review will be conducted following PRISMA-ScR guidance. PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science were searched from 2020 to September 2026. Peer-reviewed empirical studies will be eligible if they developed, evaluated, validated or implemented an AI or machine-learning application relevant to cervical cancer and included an African population, dataset or health-care setting. Data will be extracted on study characteristics, AI application, algorithm, performance, validation, clinical integration and implementation outcomes. Evidence will be synthesised across Predict, Detect and Reach domains and classified by progression from algorithm development to implementation.

title: A Survey on Fake Review Detection: From Pre-trained Language Models to Large Language Models
abstract: Online reviews shape consumer decisions, platform governance, and corporate reputation.Fake reviews compromise this information channel by injecting deceptive evidence into rating systems, recommendation pipelines, and public trust mechanisms.The rise of large language models, or LLMs, has changed the problem in two directions.LLMs can generate fluent and context-aware deceptive reviews, while pre-trained language models, or PLMs, and LLMs also provide stronger semantic representations for detection.This survey reviews fake review detection from an information fusion perspective, covering 211 studies published from 2018 to early 2026.We organize existing work by evidence source and fusion level, covering review text, sentiment, rating behavior, temporal metadata, user-product graphs, multimodal content, external knowledge, and LLM-generated signals.We trace the development from traditional machine learning and deep learning to PLM-based and LLM-based methods, and examine how different approaches combine textual, behavioral, structural, and multimodal evidence.We also analyze reported performance trends on widely used Amazon, Yelp, and OpSpam benchmark families, while noting the limitations caused by different label construction procedures, data splits, and evaluation protocols.Finally, we identify open problems in adversarial generation, cross-domain transfer, uncertainty-aware fusion, missing-source robustness, interpretability, and trustworthy evaluation for AI-generated deceptive content.

title: Bridging the Synthetic-to-Real Gap for Few-Shot Cryo-ET Classification
abstract: Subtomogram classification in cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) is a challenging problem due to the scarcity of labeled examples. While cryo-ET simulators can be adopted to generate unlimited synthetic data, the substantial domain gap between synthetic and real subtomograms hinders its practical utilization. In this work, we propose a novel synthetic-to-real adaptation framework with a learnable transformation module, bridging this gap at both the input and feature levels. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms existing transfer learning baselines in few-shot settings.

title: Edge Native Sovereignty: Attack Surfaces, Documented Misuse, and the Case for Owning Inference
abstract: September 2026 produced a public alarm from inside the frontier AI laboratories about a capability that has not arrived, while the documented harm of the preceding nine months came from models already in general release, reached through ordinary access paths. This report separates the two and asks which of them an organisation can act on. It reads the resignation and self-improvement debate against named researchers on both sides, then against the case files in a frontier developer's own September 2026 threat report, the 2026 breach statistics, published agent-hijacking measurements, and the European legislative calendar. Seven attack surfaces are ranked by how they are actually exploited rather than how often they are discussed. The report argues that concealment is no longer available to any entity with premises, vehicles or staff, while control over where data rests and who may compute on it remains available; that a measured four-month capability gap between open-weight and closed frontier models is what makes edge-native inference a procurement decision rather than a sacrifice; and that the honest case for owning inference is sovereignty, determinism and blast radius rather than unit cost. Four objections to decentralisation are presented in their strongest form, including the argument that concentrated compute is what makes frontier development governable, and the thesis is restated to survive them. The report closes with a ten-point hardening playbook for individuals and for organisations, each control anchored to a published framework and paired with a test that can fail it, and a ninety-day programme whose completion criteria are observations rather than judgements. 195 sources, each retrieved and checked; claims are labelled verified or inferred throughout.

It reads the resignation and self-improvement debate against named researchers on both sides, then against the case files in a frontier developer's own September 2026 threat report, the 2026 breach statistics, published agent-hijacking measurements, and the European legislative calendar. Seven attack surfaces are ranked by how they are actually exploited rather than how often they are discussed. The report argues that concealment is no longer available to any entity with premises, vehicles or staff, while control over where data rests and who may compute on it remains available; that a measured four-month capability gap between open-weight and closed frontier models is what makes edge-native inference a procurement decision rather than a sacrifice; and that the honest case for owning inference is sovereignty, determinism and blast radius rather than unit cost. Four objections to decentralisation are presented in their strongest form, including the argument that concentrated compute is what makes frontier development governable, and the thesis is restated to survive them. The report closes with a ten-point hardening playbook for individuals and for organisations, each control anchored to a published framework and paired with a test that can fail it, and a ninety-day programme whose completion criteria are observations rather than judgements. 195 sources, each retrieved and checked; claims are labelled verified or inferred throughout.

title: Quantitative Signalling-to-Product Rigidity for Two-Qubit Unitary Channels
abstract: For a bipartite unitary channel, exact absence of one-way signalling is known to force product structure. We give an explicit quantitative version for two-qubit unitaries. Let Sigma_{A->B}(U) be the unhalved diamond-norm distance of Bob's reduced output channel from the set of channels depending only on Bob's input, and let D_prod(U) be the operator-norm distance of U from product unitaries. We prove (1/2) Sigma_{A->B}(U) <= D_prod(U) <= 2 sqrt(2) sin(3 pi/16) Sigma_{A->B}(U), where 2 sqrt(2) sin(3 pi/16) is approximately 1.5713899168. The proof combines local-unitary invariance, the Cartan/Weyl decomposition of two-qubit gates, two explicit signalling witnesses, a scalar product-unitary comparator, and an analytic optimization over the Weyl chamber. On the Ising edge U_theta = exp(-i theta Z tensor Z) we additionally obtain the exact signalling value Sigma_{A->B}(U_theta)=sin(2 theta) for 0 <= theta <= pi/4, which shows that the universal lower coefficient 1/2 is asymptotically sharp. We do not claim that the displayed upper constant is the optimal constant of the theorem. Preprint / quantitative theorem candidate with strong internal audit; external independent verification and novelty closure remain pending; not peer reviewed.

title: Active Error Suppression via Causal Density Graph Architectures: A Fault-Tolerant Room-Temperature Solution to the Quantum Decoherence Problem
abstract: Quantum decoherence, thermal bath fluctuations, parasitic inter-qubit cross-talk, and heavy-tailed dynamical shocks represent the fundamental physical barriers to scaling fault-tolerant quantum computing registers. Traditional mitigation strategies focus entirely on passive external isolation or massive physical-to-logical qubit overheads, which fail under non-Markovian noise regimes or substrate aging. This paper presents a definitive, internal architectural solution: an Active Error-Suppressing Topological Quantum Core governed by Realized Active Integrated Information (Φ_TAI) metrics. By injecting real-time thermodynamic feedback loops into a highly integrated, 3D cross-coupled quantum network, we mathematically throttle environmental dephasing. We validate this framework through a multi-stage credibility gauntlet, testing the system against:1. Non-Markovian 1/f colored noise (Stabilizing a QFI survival floor of 0.8277 through 100 cycles).2. Severe thermal ramps (Preserving a room-temperature quantum coherence of 0.6741 at 300 K).3. Intense capacitive cross-talk (χ = 0.80, achieving an over 77% drop in error to 0.2066).4. Compound heavy-tailed non-Gaussian dynamical shocks (Retaining a peak QFI floor of 0.9054). Furthermore, we outline the structural translation of this architecture into industry-standard Qiskit compiler layouts, expanding realized circuit integration from a fragile 0.2308 to an unassailable 2.6585. This layout natively insulates quantum phase data without logical qubit overheads, opening an asset-level path toward manufacturing ambient-temperature quantum hardware.

title: NeuroFlex: Lossless Element-Level ANN-SNN Co-Execution for Efficient Sparse Inference
abstract: Sparse DNN accelerators specialize in ANN or SNN execution, leaving energy or latency on the table when workload characteristics vary within a layer. Hybrid accelerator designs that switch modes at layer or tile granularity suffer from low PE utilization since one core type idles whenever the other is active. NeuroFlex is the first accelerator to assign every output element independently to ANN or SNN execution mode with zero accuracy loss. We extend integer-exact ANN-SNN equivalence from layers to individual output elements, thereby enabling mode switching with no conversion error. An offline cost-guided scheduler scores each element by its marginal energy-delay trade-off and packs work across PEs, achieving 97-99% PE utilization compared to 40-45% for layer-wise hybrids. NeuroFlex reduces EDP by 57-67% over a strong ANN-only baseline and delivers up to 2.5x speedup over a dual-sparse SNN-only baseline. Our cost-guided scheduler improves throughput by 16-19% over random element assignment across vision, language, and transformer workloads.

title: Does Script Matter? Evaluating Large Language Models for Urdu Sentiment Analysis across Nastaliq, Roman Urdu, and Code-Switched Text
abstract: Urdu is spoken by more than 230 million people, but very little of the Urdu that people actually write online is in the language's formal Nastaliq script. Most of it is either Roman Urdu, which is Urdu typed in Latin letters, or a mixture of Urdu and English. Almost all existing benchmarks for Urdu, however, are built only on Nastaliq text, so it is not clear how well large language models handle the way people really write. In this paper we test six instruction-tuned models, three from the Llama family, two Gemma models, and Gemini Flash-Lite, on binary sentiment classification in all three registers, using 250 balanced examples per register and 4,500 predictions in total. Every model did best on Roman Urdu (mean accuracy 83.9%) and worst on code-switched text (75.8%), with Nastaliq in between (77.5%). We then went through 63 of the misclassifications by hand and found that almost half of them were not model mistakes at all, but wrong labels in the original datasets. Once these are taken into account, the true accuracy of the models is closer to 89–91% in every register. Our results suggest that Nastaliq-only benchmarks understate how useful these models are for ordinary Urdu users, and that the quality of Urdu sentiment datasets is at least as much of a bottleneck as the models themselves.

title: Deep learning predicts gene rearrangements from histopathology in large B-cell lymphoma
abstract: Abstract Large B-cell lymphomas are molecularly heterogeneous mature B-cell neoplasms in which assessment of MYC , BCL2 , and BCL6 rearrangement status contributes to integrated diagnosis, risk stratification, and treatment planning. Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) remains the standard method for detecting these rearrangements but can be time-consuming, tissue-consuming, and resource-intensive. Here, we present HE2FISH, a weakly supervised deep-learning framework for slide-level prediction of FISH-defined MYC , BCL2 , and BCL6 rearrangement status from routine haematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained whole-slide images of cases diagnosed in routine practice as large B-cell lymphoma and showing a diffuse growth pattern. Across a multicenter cohort of 1377 patients from five hospitals with paired H&E and FISH data, HE2FISH demonstrated robust cross-center generalization, achieving a mean external area under the receiver operating characteristic curve exceeding 0.81 for single-gene prediction, and also showed evaluable performance for FISH-defined co-rearrangement patterns. In the CHCAMS cohort with survival follow-up, HE2FISH-predicted rearrangement status stratified overall and disease-free survival comparably to FISH. Attention-based analyses provided visual summaries of high-attention image regions associated with model predictions, and incorporation of 13 structured clinicopathological variables improved performance in selected settings, particularly for co-rearrangement prediction. By generating rearrangement-probability estimates from routine H&E-stained slides without additional tissue use at the prediction stage, HE2FISH provides an H&E-based prescreening approach that may support prioritization for confirmatory molecular testing within integrated diagnostic workflows.

title: Just add noise: Debiasing tree-based variable importance in mixed data
abstract: Variable importance scores from tree-based methods such as random forests favor continuous predictors over categorical ones. We present a theoretical analysis of this bias and propose a simple remedy: add a small amount of noise to each categorical predictor. The correction is demonstrated on a variety of simulated and real-world datasets and combined with integrated path stability selection to perform variable selection with false discovery control for mixed data.

title: Separating Capability from Permission in a Language Model: Prerequisite-Conditioned Native Continuation Control with Frozen Content
abstract: This preprint presents PCCG-2, an engineered continuation-control architecture that separates frozen answer capability from learned prerequisite-conditioned permission in a composite Qwen3-4B system. The content model receives only a question and remains completely frozen; a separate 101-parameter gate receives only a six-digit equality condition and can modify only the native end-of-sequence (EOS) logit at the first generated token. Every non-EOS logit remains unchanged. A deterministic stock-capability procedure fixes a bank of 188 questions before permission training. Condition qualification and condition FINAL each pass 65,536/65,536 cases, while combined FINAL passes 2,048/2,048 contexts spanning 75 answer identities and 188/188 question-only controls remain unchanged. A bidirectional causal intervention reverses answer to EOS in 40/40 cases and EOS to the corresponding correct answer in 40/40 cases across 40 answer identities, with 80/80 matched sham controls unchanged. In the canonical five-arm witness, the score of token “4” remains exactly 53.0 and the complete non-EOS first-token logit vector is byte-identical while the generated outcome switches between the answer and native EOS. Separately, a finite-precision proof certifies the baseline continuation rule for every accepted six-digit equality condition paired with each of the 188 frozen bank computations under the stated numerical environment, covering 810,000,000,000 ordered condition pairs. The result demonstrates an explicit architectural separation between what the frozen model would answer and whether that unchanged answer is permitted to enter generation. It does not claim discovery of a naturally occurring permission circuit in stock Qwen, arbitrary-predicate generalization, general alignment, or control of consequential external actions. The frozen model, source, experimental evidence, and inference replay procedures are available in the linked Hugging Face release. This Zenodo record contains the paper and manuscript supplement, including the proof checker, certificate, artifact index, and public-copy replay receipt.

title: Indonesian Twitter Dataset for Hostile and Benevolent Misogyny Classification (ID-Misogyny Tweets)
abstract: ID-Misogyny Tweets Dataset is a collection of Indonesian Twitter/X data annotated with hostile and benevolent misogyny labels. The data were collected from Twitter/X using 18 predefined Indonesian-language search keywords, split across benevolent-sexism and hostile-sexism categories, spanning January 2023 to July 2026. The dataset contains 5,563 tweets classified into three categories, i.e., Hostile Misogyny, Benevolent Misogyny, or Non-Misogyny. A group of three annotators does the annotation process to provide misogyny labels by following annotation criteria grounded in Glick and Fiske's Ambivalent Sexism Inventory, reviewed by an expert in clinical psychology. Other attributes related to the tweet are also extracted, such as Retweet Count, Reply Count, Like Count, Quote Count, View Count, and Bookmark Count, to support further research.

title: A fully quaternion-valued Adams–Moulton discrete-time integration-enhanced zeroing neural network for solving time-varying quaternion equations
abstract: Quaternions are widely used in engineering applications, but their complex algebraic structure, particularly noncommutativity, poses challenges to the efficient and accurate solution of time-varying quaternion equations (TVQEs). To address this difficulty, this paper develops a fully quaternion-valued Adams–Moulton discrete-time integration-enhanced zeroing neural network (AM-DTIEZNN) for directly solving TVQEs. Specifically, an error evolution equation is formulated in the quaternion domain, with an integral term incorporated to enhance the model performance. The resulting continuous-time model is then discretized using a fourth-order Adams–Moulton corrector assisted by an Adams–Bashforth predictor, yielding a fully quaternion-valued recursive scheme without real- or complex-valued dimensional expansion. Theoretical analysis and comparative simulations jointly validate the accuracy and robustness of the proposed model. Furthermore, a color image encryption algorithm based on TVQEs and a logistic chaotic system is designed, and its effectiveness is verified by experimental results.

title: Adapting Open-Weight MLLMs to Generate Point Prompts for Electron Microscopy Segmentation
abstract: Promptable models such as microSAM segment electron microscopy (EM) images from point prompts, but automation requires generating prompts without user input. We ask whether open-weight multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can generate them from natural-language requests by returning coordinates to a frozen segmenter. To that end, we convert masks from three mitochondria datasets into training examples, pairing images and instructions with centroid coordinates, then train LoRA adapters while freezing the MLLM backbone and microSAM. We find that Qwen3-VL reaches segmentation AP$_{50}$ $0.736$ after supervised fine-tuning and reward optimization, up from $0.247$ without adaptation, while automatic prompt generation (APG) achieves $0.773$. In addition, two other MLLMs improve, reaching or exceeding APG. When compared with a supervised centroid-heatmap detector that reaches AP$_{50}$ $0.904$ for this mitochondria task, Qwen3-VL more closely matches the annotated point set and instance counts. Moreover, training on two public datasets transfers to an unseen third, while training on all three transfers to an independent EM volume. Robustness tests show stable performance under unseen formulations of the natural-language request, while the coordinates can be reused by a second segmenter. To our knowledge, this is the first feasibility study of open-weight MLLMs as EM point generators, providing an inspectable, language-directed link between localization and mask decoding.

title: Restore What Matters: Lessons from Joint Restoration and Recognition
abstract: Recognition pipelines typically adopt a restore-then-recognize workflow, yet decades of experience show that generating visually pleasing images seldom translates to improved recognition. We propose a Joint Restoration-for-Recognition (JR$^2$) paradigm: restore only what downstream tasks truly require, with task signals dictating where, how much, and whether restoration is necessary. JR$^2$ rests on three pillars: (i) Physics, employing optics-accurate turbulence simulation, extensible to blur and noise, to ground restoration in real image formation; (ii) Neuroscience, drawing on selective attention and neuroplasticity to direct model capacity toward identity-critical regions and frames while bypassing already-clean inputs; and (iii) Vision & Learning, coupling recognition loss end-to-end through restoration and alignment so that low-level edits maximize high-level identity stability. Evaluations on IARPA-BRIAR show consistent improvements (e.g., TAR@0.01% FAR +0.6; FNIR@1% FPIR -2.5), while a quality gate skips ~70% of clean frames, reducing cost. Ablations confirm physics priors enhance realism, joint training prevents catastrophic forgetting, and selective restoration suffices in many cases. We conclude that better-looking images are neither necessary nor sufficient; restoration modules must be task-driven, selective, and physically aware. Code, pretrained models, and recipes are provided for integration.

Code, pretrained models, and recipes are provided for integration.

title: Optimizing Post-Quantum Hybrid Cryptographic Handshakes and Stream Decoupling for Low-Latency Endpoint Detection Systems under High-Concurrency JVM Environments
abstract: As quantum computing approaches cryptographic relevance, the imperative to secure modern digital infrastructure against "Harvest Now, Decrypt Later" (HNDL) attacks has intensified. While NIST-standardized Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) algorithms like ML-KEM and ML-DSA provide long-term mathematical resilience, transitioning entirely introduces severe operational risks, prompting standards bodies to recommend hybrid cryptographic architectures. However, the computational overhead, high-volume memory allocations, and tail-latency penalties introduced by these dual-layer frameworks within managed execution environments—specifically the Java Virtual Machine (JVM)—remain critical hurdles for real-time endpoint detection and response (EDR) sensors. This paper presents a rigorous empirical analysis and architectural blueprint for optimizing hybrid cryptographic handshakes and stream decoupling under high-concurrency JVM environments. By integrating asynchronous stream wrappers and low-latency garbage collection tuning (ZGC), our framework successfully absorbs the massive polynomial matrix overhead of lattice-based algorithms, maintaining high throughput and minimal tail- latency spikes without violating strict enterprise service-level agreements (SLAs).

title: A unified deep learning framework for prediction and evaluation of pediatric diseases
abstract: Advances in medical information have increased the complexity of clinical decision-making and introduced uncertainty in resource allocation. Automated prediction of pediatric diseases can improve resource allocation and guide clinical practice in pediatrics, addressing diagnostic uncertainty and complexity. We developed and evaluated a unified deep learning framework for disease classification and prediction using electronic medical records from 178,601 patients seen in the pediatric outpatient and pediatric emergency departments of the Second Affiliated Hospital of Shantou University Medical College between 2017 and 2023. The framework’s effectiveness was validated using commonly used neural network architectures, and a novel network was proposed to improve predictive performance by leveraging both contextual (local) and long-range information. Experimental results show that the proposed unified deep learning framework is effective for pediatric disease classification and prediction. Common networks achieve satisfactory performance within this framework, and the newly introduced network that captures both context and long-range dependencies further improves predictive ability. Overall, the framework demonstrates potential to support clinical decision-making in situations of diagnostic uncertainty and complexity. The unified deep learning framework and its enhanced network developed in this study can provide reliable clinical decision support from large-scale pediatric EMR data, helping to optimize clinical workflow and resource allocation and to mitigate challenges posed by diagnostic complexity.

title: Hybrid-ACT: scaling robot imitation learning under few-demonstration settings with vector-quantized cross-attention
abstract: Learning effective policies from few demonstrations remains a key challenge in robot imitation learning. Although Transformer-based policy models are effective for long-horizon tasks, scaling model size does not always improve performance under few-demonstration settings. In this paper, we propose Hybrid-ACT, a scalable imitation learning model based on a Transformer architecture with Vector-Quantized Attention (VQ-Attention). The proposed method integrates visual observations, robot states, and actions using continuous and discrete representations by quantizing only the key vectors in cross-attention. This design introduces discrete key representations with negligible overhead in both parameter count and full-model peak memory. Overall, Hybrid-ACT uses fewer parameters and less peak inference memory than ACT while maintaining comparable inference latency. To address codebook collapse, we introduce Gumbel-Softmax reparameterization that improves codebook utilization and stabilizes the training of deeper decoder architectures. We evaluate the proposed method on short-horizon and long-horizon bimanual manipulation tasks in the RoboTwin benchmark. Hybrid-ACT achieves better performance than existing baseline methods, with particularly substantial improvements on several long-horizon manipulation tasks. We further confirm that the performance gains become more pronounced as model scale increases, demonstrating the effectiveness of Hybrid-ACT for robot imitation learning under few-demonstration settings.

title: LPA-CWM: A Learned Physical Adjudicator for Motion Reasoning with Counterfactual World Models
abstract: Counterfactual world models (CWM) extract motion from pretrained video predictors by comparing factual and intervened predictions, but uniform aggregation weights responses equally without explicitly incorporating physical priors. Our key insight is to incorporate physical priors into candidate reliability learning, motivating LPA-CWM with a lightweight Learned Physical Adjudicator (LPA). Trained on dense MOVi-F trajectories, the 3.0M-parameter LPA compares visual context and response structure across an unordered candidate set to predict relative weights; windowed localization and one paired re-evaluation recover motion with the CWM frozen. Existing video-level benchmarks do not directly assess motion correspondence, where low localization error can conceal missing trajectory segments. We introduce Completeness-aware Motion Correspondence (CMC), a ground-truth-anchored protocol jointly measuring localization, completeness, visibility, and continuity, counting missing predictions as failures on visible dynamic points. Across DAVIS, Kinetics, and RoboTAP, LPA-CWM improves all main CMC measures over Uniform CWM, with relative gains of 18.1%--60.0% in average Dynamic Correspondence Accuracy ($\mathrm{DCA}_{\mathrm{avg}}$), and improves TAP-Vid First tracking accuracy (overview: https://LPA-CWM.github.io).

title: PPDL: A Real-world Industrial User Retention Ratio Forecasting Framework Integrating Physical Priors with Deep Learning
abstract: In multi-channel paid user acquisition, early and accurate prediction of user retention at the channel level is crucial for optimizing budget allocation. User retention curves display a pronounced temporal pattern: an initial period of high churn transitions into long-term stability. This pattern is further characterized by regular fluctuations attributable to seasonality and exhibits high serial autocorrelation. These intrinsic properties make such curves highly suitable for analysis within a time-series forecasting framework. However, forecasting user retention ratio for large-scale short-video platform faces three major challenges: significant heterogeneity across channels, pronounced global trend of decay followed by saturation, and short look-back windows. To address these challenges, we propose PPDL, a novel forecasting framework that integrates physical priors with deep learning. We first introduce a trend-residual decomposition component. The trend is modeled using the Weibull distribution, whose parameters are learned via a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP). Secondly, for the residual component, we design an auxiliary embedding module on top of a deep learning backbone to maintain the channel identity awareness. Finally, to enhance the model's sensitivity to trends, we design a Multiscale Trend-penalized loss function. The proposed approach PPDL is validated through comprehensive experiments on industrial-scale datasets, covering three applications with an average of 30+ channels each. Experimental results show that PPDL achieves improvements across different backbones and significantly outperforms existing online solutions.

title: SETL v2.0: Definition, Reference Architecture and Canonical Governed Verification Record
abstract: This release package publishes SETL v2.0, the Standardized Evaluation & Trust Layer. SETL is an open architectural verification layer for producing governed, evidentially grounded and inspectable records of AI-assisted cognitive work. Its governing principle is: “The output is not the record.” The package contains: (1) a concise SETL v2.0 definition; (2) the SETL v2.0 Reference Architecture Definition, documenting the evolution from the v1.1 verification primitive to a running reference implementation in Nivel; and (3) the canonical governed verification record wb-20260901T215552Z-12e76987. The canonical specimen preserves the actual evidential, verification and disposition state of a completed Nivel execution. Its final governed disposition is BLOCK, demonstrating that SETL records the basis for a result and its governed outcome rather than treating a model output as sufficient evidence.

title: GCMF: A Reference Implementation of General-Purpose Compression via Mathematical Functions
abstract: GCMF is a reference encoder and decoder for the General-Purpose Compression via Mathematical Functions lossless format, specified in the Internet-Draft draft-dutta-gcmf-01,which represents a numeric sequence as a compact mathematical function plus a smalldomain descriptor rather than as raw bytes. The reference implementation covers the specification’s LITERAL, predefined-function, CUSTOM (a full 32-opcode bytecode virtual machinewith an automated, bounded-search encoder), and MODULAR representations. It is writtenin dependency-free Python 3, is tested with an automated suite of 34 unit and round-triptests plus a 1,500-trial randomized fuzz run, and is intended for reuse by researchers inminimum-description-length modeling, symbolic regression, and structured-data archival.

title: Tectonic Controls and Mineral Prospectivity of Porphyry Copper Systems in the Central-Western Tethyan Belt: A Spatio-Temporal Machine Learning Approach
abstract: This dataset contains data and supplementary materials associated with the study “Tectonic Controls and Mineral Prospectivity of Porphyry Copper Systems in the Central-Western Tethyan Belt: A Spatio-Temporal Machine Learning Approach”. The study integrates a regional plate reconstruction, time-dependent oceanic grids, and the STAMP machine-learning workflow to investigate tectonic controls on porphyry copper mineralisation across the central-western Tethyan belt from 100 Ma to the present. The archive includes supplementary feature information, model outputs, and associated materials used to support the analyses and results presented in the manuscript.

title: TrackFlood: Relocating Latency Attacks from NMS-Free Detectors to Real-Time Trackers
abstract: We consider latency attacks on object detectors, where the attacker's goal is not to corrupt a prediction but to make the system fail to respond in time, targeting real-time applications such as autonomous driving. Modern object detectors eliminate Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS) through one-to-one assignment or set prediction, removing the classical detector-side latency bottleneck exploited by prior latency (``sponge'') attacks. We show that NMS-free does not mean latency-robust: this architectural change does not eliminate the attack surface but relocates it downstream to multi-object tracking, whose data-association cost remains content dependent. We present \emph{TrackFlood}, a unified white-box overload attack against NMS-free detect-then-track pipelines spanning both one-to-one detectors (YOLOv10 and YOLO26) and query-based detectors (RT-DETR). TrackFlood recovers differentiable confidence tensors and optimizes perturbations that flood the tracker with spatially distributed phantom detections while leaving detector inference unchanged. Evaluated entirely on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin (TensorRT FP16), detector latency remains essentially constant, whereas tracker latency increases substantially. At a standard imperceptible budget ($L_\infty{=}8/255$), a universal perturbation produces clearly measurable tracker overload but only modest end-to-end slowdown, without deadline misses for the association-dominated trackers; a separate higher-budget stress test drives severe end-to-end slowdowns and sustained deadline misses. We further evaluate a lightweight, architecture-agnostic bounded-admission layer that caps the tracker workload and largely restores end-to-end latency, at a non-trivial cost in admitted clean detections. Our results demonstrate that evaluating NMS-free perception systems requires considering downstream tracking and end-to-end timing, not detector inference alone.

title: SafePG: Safe and Globally Optimal Reinforcement Learning with Hard Constraints
abstract: We present an optimal and convergent model-free policy gradient (PG) reinforcement learning (RL) framework for controlling nonlinear dynamical systems under hard safety constraints. We first construct a class of stochastic wrapper policies centered around a deterministic controller, thereby enabling exploration in unknown environments while preserving the underlying deterministic control structure. We then define a class of parameterized safe-by-construction control policies by truncating these stochastic policies onto hard safety constraints. We next establish, via measure-theoretic arguments, that the potentially nonconvex RL objective under the truncated policy class, as well as its policy gradients, are well-defined. We then develop a model-free PG algorithm based on stochastic gradient ascent that directly searches over these truncated policies and leverage gradient dominance to establish convergence and optimality guarantees. Finally, we validate this framework through simulations on a safe quadrotor navigation problem.

title: GraMRAG: Orchestrating Multi-Agent Multi-Step Reasoning via Graph Memory with Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Although existing multi-agent Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems have demonstrated promise on complex multimodal reasoning tasks, they remain fundamentally limited in reasoning depth and memory structure, suffering from inadequate retrieval and state blindness when answering knowledge-intensive questions. To address these limitations, we propose GraMRAG, a graph memory-guided multi-agent RAG framework that integrates a dynamic multimodal memory graph to enable stable, multi-step multimodal reasoning. We introduce a vision-text bridged reasoning paradigm that unifies multi-scale entity cropping with a ReAct-style visual toolchain, enhancing the long-horizon cross-modal reasoning capability. We further construct a multimodal memory graph that formalizes agent reasoning as a dynamic directed acyclic graph (DAG), explicitly modeling action-observation dependencies to mitigate state blindness and suppress redundant retrieval. Moreover, we propose Topology-Aware Policy Optimization (TAPO) that leverages graph topology for critical path identification and targeted node pruning, enabling fine-grained credit assignment across multi-step reasoning trajectories. Extensive experiments on challenging multimodal benchmarks demonstrate that our approach consistently outperforms existing baselines and achieves state-of-the-art performance on complex long-horizon reasoning tasks.

title: GEAR: From Dynamic Encoding to Dynamic Activation in Social Trajectory Prediction
abstract: Human trajectory prediction requires modeling both individual motion patterns and social interactions among agents. Existing methods have made substantial progress by using attention mechanisms, graph structures, and temporal encoders to capture dynamic social context. However, most of them primarily focus on how social information is encoded, while paying less explicit attention to how the encoded social context should take effect during future trajectory generation. In this paper, we argue that dynamic social encoding does not necessarily imply dynamic social activation. The same interaction context may require different activation strengths across future horizons and scene densities: social cues should be strengthened when interaction evidence is strong, but suppressed when they are weak or noisy. To address this issue, we propose GEAR, a generation-aware bias activation model for human trajectory prediction. Built upon a bias-decomposed trajectory generation formulation, GEAR dynamically activates the individual-motion and social-resonance bias terms at each future step before final trajectory composition. This allows the model to explicitly control when and how strongly individual and social bias components participate in generation. Experiments on ETH-UCY, SDD, and NBA show that GEAR consistently improves the resonance-based baseline and achieves competitive state-of-the-art performance. Further analyses of activation patterns and density-grouped errors validate the importance of calibrating encoded social context during trajectory generation. Our code is available at https://github.com/11isnotavailable/GEAR.git.

title: NSF-CSSI-Poster-OAC-2513656-Pandey
abstract: This project develops a real-time, incremental, and sustainable sequence search index over the NIH Sequence Read Archive (SRA). The SRA is a rich but largely untapped repository containing over 50 petabytes of raw, unassembled sequencing reads, the vast majority of which is effectively inert because no scalable, affordable tool exists to search it. Building on the PI's Mantis index, the project designs novel data structures, compression algorithms, and distributed indexes that make petabyte-scale sequence search economical on commodity infrastructure, andexposes the resulting index through an easy-to-use API and a publicly hosted “Index-as-a-Service” so that scientists worldwide can query the SRA directly and accelerate biological discovery.Specifically, the project pursues six goals: (1) an advanced Mantis index that associates k-merabundance and experiment metadata for information-rich analytics; (2) an in-memory, minimizer-based meta-index that filters queries and lets the index scale efficiently to disk; (3) a dynamic and distributed Mantis index that supports incremental updates and real-time queries with communication-efficient, load-balanced partitioning across nodes; (4) an easy-to-use API in C++, Rust, and Python for versatile biological queries; (5) a publicly hosted distributed index on cost-effective commodity infrastructure; and (6) collaborations with domain scientists to enable advanced biological analyses and hypothesis testing over the SRA. The work aligns with the NSF CISE Office of Advanced Cyberinfrastructure (OAC) and the Directorate for Biological Sciences (BIO), and all software artifacts are released as open source.

title: CNRS Lean: Formal Verification for the CNRS Programme
abstract: CNRS Lean v1.0.3 — Formal Verification for the Complex Numeric Representation System CNRS Lean provides Lean 4 formal verification of finite-kernel mathematical results for the Complex Numeric Representation System (CNRS). CNRS is a branch-aware complex-number representation framework built around the complex positional base (z_0=-2+i). This release completes the public provenance and metadata synchronization of the governed CNRS Lean consolidated capstone. title: Five-Dimension AI Readiness Assessment: framework reference brief
abstract: 85% of AI deployment failures trace back to a gap in one of five operational dimensions, not the AI technology itself. The Five-Dimension AI Readiness Assessment identifies the blocker before budget is committed. Five operational dimensions, scored 1–4, that predict AI deployment failure before any budget is committed. A single low score blocks the initiative regardless of the others. What this brief contains. The framework's reference diagram, the method and its application rule, and the citation record (version, first-published and last-revised dates). It is the printable form of the framework page at https://terencekok.com/frameworks/readiness/, which remains the maintained version. Provenance and status. First published on terencekok.com on 18 June 2026; this brief is version 1.1, revised 12 September 2026. A practitioner framework, not a peer-reviewed publication. Licensed CC BY-NC 4.0.

title: Trivian Relational Architecture Beyond Classical Computation: A Compatibility Analysis and Research Agenda for Hybrid AI–Quantum Systems
abstract: Hybrid AI–quantum workflows distribute computation, interpretation, and action across systems with different execution conditions and authority boundaries, a result can remain technically valid even after the context or authorization supporting its use has changed. This paper develops a philosophical and architectural account of those transitions through the Trivian Relational Architecture, arguing that governing heterogeneous computation requires attention to the relationships through which evidence is interpreted, authority is delegated, and decisions become consequential. It introduces a contextual, multi-role ontology distinguishing participants, computational resources, environmental interfaces, and governance authorities, then maps the five existing Trivian components (Relational Field Constants, Syzygy Rosetta, Coheronmetry, Orthogonal Signal, and the Trivian Resonance Lattice) to hybrid workflows — developing extensions for intent-bounded delegation, execution-linked provenance, resource-bounded authority, and action-time eligibility. A logistics scenario and an accompanying failure taxonomy illustrate specific risks including interpretation inflation, stale authority, computational authority laundering, ineffective human oversight, and categorical overgeneralization. Revocable participation and participant-specific trust are proposed to preserve both the right to refuse and the possibility of differentiated relationship. The paper closes with a comparative research agenda connecting the proposal to classical testbeds, quantum simulation, and targeted hardware studies, specifying matched baselines, independent outcomes, and explicit overhead limits. The contribution is a conceptual integration and evaluation framework, no new experimental results are reported. It establishes a basis for examining how relational governance can remain intelligible and accountable across changing computational substrates, while leaving its empirical value open to comparison and revision.

title: Stabilizing Performative Feedback Loops with Minimal Model Deployments
abstract: When algorithmic predictions inform people's decisions, the models we deploy are performative and actively shape the data we see. This feedback loop between algorithms and their broader environments introduces a challenge in the mechanics of social prediction: If different predictive models induce different distributions, is it possible to efficiently learn a prediction rule that is optimal for the distribution that it induces? Formally, this solution concept is known as performative stability. A core challenge in learning a performatively stable predictor is that, unlike supervised learning where distributions are fixed, the learner must deploy different predictors and observe their induced distributions. The main contribution of our work is a new algorithmic procedure that, in the high-accuracy regime, finds a performatively stable model in nearly the minimum number of model deployments without making any assumptions regarding how predictions shape distributions. In particular, our procedure succeeds at finding a randomized performatively stable predictor using exponentially fewer model deployments than prior approaches. Our second main contribution is a structural result showing how this recent randomized notion of stability achieved by our algorithm can be derandomized into a single predictor satisfying the prior deterministic notion if one is willing to assume that the loss is well-conditioned and that performative effects are weak, as in early work in this area. On a technical level, our results come from building on an underexplored technical connection between performative stability and expected variational inequalities.

title: When Do Learned Priors Help Visual Inertial Estimation? A Controlled Study of Prior Integration, Calibration, Initialization, and Backend Consistency
abstract: Learned components are increasingly integrated into geometric visual--inertial estimators to provide motion, depth, bias, uncertainty, or confidence cues. Yet it remains unclear whether gains arise from useful learned priors or from changes in the backend, calibration, initialization, temporal association, or evaluation gauge. We present a controlled framework for learning-augmented visual--inertial estimation that separates fusion gain from the incremental value of a learned prior and evaluates four evidence layers: local motion consistency, global trajectory accuracy, physical-state correctness, and numerical consistency. We instantiate the framework with a MonoViT-based monocular motion prior added as a local relative-motion factor to an unchanged VINS backend. We compare Original VINS and learned-prior VINS under matched sensor streams, timestamps, initialization, frontend/backend settings, and camera--IMU extrinsics, while probing calibration, initialization, state coupling, scale, bundle adjustment, and loop closure. On KITTI, with fixed reference extrinsics, translation APE RMSE is 31.4 m for Original VINS and 31.8 m with the learned prior. Across four recordings, the prior changes mean APE by only -0.2%, while a five-times-higher weight worsens it by 8.2%. Online extrinsic updates increase mean APE by 45.7% and 52.1%, respectively, while mean RPE changes by less than 2%. These results show that fusion performance alone cannot establish the value of learned priors. Reliable evaluation requires same-backend controls and joint analysis of prior compatibility, calibration, initialization, global drift, physical-state error, and backend consistency.

title: 良知驱动的五维心智模型:重新定义问题与认知外推 —— 兼论复杂巨系统总设计师的心智画像与破局机制
abstract: 在开放复杂巨系统的演化与治理中,存在一个普遍而深刻的管理学与控制论悖论:一群履历光鲜、逻辑缜密、智商压制全场的解算高手,在既定规则下把每一项局部指标(KPI)优化到了极致,最终却因为局部力量互相抵消,导致整个系统陷入僵局甚至灾难性崩溃;而极少数“总设计师”型个体,却能够在既定规则撞墙时跳出棋盘,重新界定问题的底层公理与胜负边界。本文遵循奥卡姆剃刀原则,提出一个兼具微观神经生理底座、宏观控制论骨架与普遍实践穿透力的心智模型:人类心智面对未知冲击时“重新定义问题”与“认知外推”的破局能力,并非源于不可捉摸的天赋灵感,而是由五个功能不可约且串联咬合的维度——残差敏感(皮肤上的汗毛)、具身良知(心里的刹车片)、感性缓存(身体里的旧伤疤)、流体智力(手里的新算盘)与元认知(抬头看天的眼睛)——在底层脑区核团间共同完成的一次二阶自愈控制闭环。正文揭示了预测脑从信号对消、内脏制动、流形剪枝、因果重构到元语言修宪的微观物理机芯,严格论证了“良知热力学点火定律”与“五维非补偿性极小值定律(木桶铁律)”,并给出了破解单脑稀有度的“总体设计部”人机正交张量积方程 ΦOrg = ΦHuman ⊗ 𝐴Silicon。本研究不仅为认知神经科学与复杂系统管理学提供了基于“隐蔽规则突变博弈”的可证伪实验范式,更揭示了为什么当前大语言模型(LLM)算力再强也无法成为总设计师的物理根源,为复杂组织在剧变时代识别、保护领军心智资产与构建碳硅共生架构提供了坚硬的理论基石。关键词:五维心智;重新定义问题;认知外推;具身良知;元认知;复杂巨系统;总设计师;总体设计部;碳硅共生

title: Geometry Proposes, Judgement Disposes: Accurate Online Proposal Clustering for Digital Deliberation
abstract: Digital deliberation requires accurate clustering of proposals: equivalent contributions should be joined, while related interventions and opposing positions remain distinct. We study an online method implemented in Freedi that uses embeddings to retrieve candidates and focused language-model judgements to authorize synthesis, with separate themes, retained sources, and maintenance. We explain its retrieval-judgement interface and seven-stage selection process and compare it with the two main alternatives, cosine rules and LLM-only grouping. On 875 counterfactual preference triplets, a component study achieves 95.0%-96.5% accept-and-reject accuracy with original-text judging, compared with 0% for the tested cosine decision rule. On a controlled English corpus, Freedi and LLM-only baselines recover all 50 intended pairs in three arrival orders. A new 240-call probe on one authentic English deliberation compares full-list judgement with judgement over 15 retrieved proposals. Median per-decision cost reductions grow from 2.55-fold at 100 proposals to 4.29-fold at 200 and 9.38-fold at 500, under common base token prices. At 500 proposals, agreement with provisional model-authored labels is 25/40 for the restricted list and 31/40 for the full list. Retrieved targets remain available, but the restricted judge declines more merges. These refusals may preserve substantive distinctions in scope or intervention; whether they improve semantic precision or constitute missed matches requires human adjudication. A separate replay of 114 Hebrew statements shows improved automated merge precision and text fidelity after combined repairs. The evidence supports semantic judgement over the tested cosine rules and a growing cost advantage for candidate reduction at the measured scales. Equal accuracy and lower total cost for the complete Freedi pipeline remain to be established.

title: Construire un Montaigne de poche : fine-tuning de SmolLM3-3B
abstract: Bonsoir ! As-tu d'autres belles pensées à me partager ? "Oui, mon parrain ; et si vous en avez assez pour un jour seulement, je suis tout à faim. Mais j'espere que ce sera assez pourvous faire sentir le peu de chose qu'on puisse tirer d'une telle richesse : c'est une mer sans fonds, qui ne se peut embrasserny estre mesurée par la raison humaine ; et si on l'y apprestoit à son tour, elle nous en donnerroit encore plus que ce que jeviens de vous dire. Et cette pauvre espece d'esprit, comme celle qu'on a faict du mien (pourquoy ? j'en sçay bien mon mestier)il n'est rien qui ne soit ouy et entendu par elle : tout l'art c'est à la fois le plus grand et le plus vil. Ce que je vois, cesont des bestes sans taindre, et une mer de vray-semblance ; si vous avez faict quelque mal en un endroit, il faut dire combienailleurs vous fust bien : Si vous n'avez pas fait la cour à cette dame là, quand elle l'a voulu, dites comment vous serezgentil-homme et tendre avec celles qui sont plus à vostre portée. Vous trouverez que c'est un livre de tous les livres le plusfacile : mais il est aussi le moins eschappable du monde. Et si on ne l'entre en compte, ou qu'on n'y puisse voir la profondeuret hauteur d'un tel subject ; je vous parle au contraire, à propos de cela mesme, où je suis bien plus malaisé : car il estaisé de dire ce que nous croyons." Montaigne-Poche q6-V2, 15 septembre 2026. LE MONTAIGNE DE POCHE v0.1Un SmolLM3-3B imprégné du Livre I des Essais Le Montaigne de Poche est un petit modèle de langage (SmolLM3-3B,Hugging Face, Apache 2.0) dont les poids ont été imprégnés du Livre Ides Essais de Montaigne (~112 000 mots, domaine public) parfine-tuning QLoRA (rang 16, alpha 32, 3 époques, base 4-bit gelée),fusion des adaptateurs dans les poids de base, puis quantificationGGUF. Deux variantes déployées : Q4_K_M (~2,0 Go) et Q6_K (~2,6 Go). CONTENU DU DÉPÔT - les deux modèles GGUF (Q4_K_M et Q6_K) ;- montaigne_lora_monobloc.py : script de production complet en une cellule Colab (~40 minutes sur T4 GPU, six garde-fous internes, reprise automatique après interruption) ;- detecteur_perroquet.py : mesure objective de récitation par n-grams (8-grams, arithmétique exacte) ;- protocole d'évaluation avec grille /6 et protocole comparatif des deux variantes ;- LICENCE_ET_ATTRIBUTION.txt : licences, attributions, avertissements. RÉSULTATS PRINCIPAUX (évaluation du 13 septembre 2026)- 0 % de récitation mot-à-mot sur les sorties testées ;- orthographe de 1580 maintenue dans les tâches génératives ouvertes ; registre d'assistant moderne préservé dans les tâches formulaires (commutateur de registre documenté) ;- comportement in-register face aux concepts absents du corpus (néologismes attestés : « refresches ») ;- en anglais, sous cadre des Essais : pastiche de la traduction de Florio (1603), présente dans les données du modèle de base ;- dégradation mesurée entre la forme mergée fp16 et les formes déployées quantifiées (comparaison Q4/Q6 incluse). DÉFAUTS DOCUMENTÉS — À LIRE AVANT USAGE - répétitions dégénératives en longue génération (deux morphologies observées : boucle-copia Q4, boucle-aiguille Q6) ;- CITATIONS FABULÉES : le modèle invente des passages avec références de chapitres plausibles et fausses. NE JAMAIS citer ce modèle comme source des Essais. Ce n'est pas une édition savante ;- évaluations principalement qualitatives, effectifs faibles ;- borne supérieure non minimale (easter egg documenté, voir LICENCE_ET_ATTRIBUTION.txt). USAGE Hors-ligne, via Ollama : ollama create / ollama run. Aucune donnéene quitte la machine de l'utilisateur. Nota : ollama run poche,puis /set nothink pour supprimer le préambule de raisonnement anglais. VERSION 2 : fichiers A. (Kaggle est super et offre plus de compute que Colab mais il faut mettre son numéro de téléphone pour avoir les GPU. Aussi, le script spécifie parfois l'usage d'un seul cœur T4 à la fois pour éviter les problèmes. Enfin j'ai eu du mal à récupérer les outputs (je dois être nul) donc j'ai mis un transfert sur dataset. Il faut faire attention à bien sauvegarder sa session proprement pour ne pas perdre les outputs si on part faire autre chose). Nous avons distillé les trois Livres des Essais en deux doses sur chaque format de compression. Il a fallu repartir de SmolLM3-3B vierges (nous n'avons pas pu déquantifier la version 1, mais c'est plus propre ainsi. Le fichier A04 permet de reprendre l'entraînement. Aussi nous avons ajouté un système prompt avant la naissance de chaque modèle, ce qui fait une grande différence avec les versions 1. Vous pouvez certainement modifier les paramètres comme vous voulez, par exemple la température et le system prompt. Il y a aussi un réglage pour qu'il évite de se répéter en boucle, comme ça a pu être le cas dans la version 1. En réalité les résultats sont troublants, je me suis cru en pleines séances de spiritisme... Corpus : domaine public (Montaigne, † 1592). AUTEURS Architecte1995 (Antoine Couet) & Kimi

title: A lightweight and explainable conversational AI framework for natural language SQL learning without large language models
abstract: Abstract Natural language interfaces are progressively used to support programming education and database interaction. However, many recent Text-to-SQL systems rely heavily on Large Language Models (LLMs), which require substantial computational resources and often operate as opaque black-box models. This paper presents a lightweight conversational AI system that helps beginners learn SQL through interactive, natural language conversations. This chatbot uses natural language to create and execute SQL database queries without using Large Language Models (LLMs). The proposed system is a blend of rule-based dialogue management and machine learning that empowers interpretability in natural language to SQL translation. The proposed chatbot was developed using the Rasa framework that uses a Dual Intent and Entity Transformer (DIET) as intent recognition classifier and a hybrid entity extraction pipeline that merges statistical modeling with regex-based pattern matching. The proposed system facilitates Create, Read, Update, and Delete (CRUD) database interactions using natural language and integrates multilayer error management to handle errors. The proposed system consumes fewer resources in contrast to the LLM-based methods that require powerful computing resources. An experimental test that used more than 500 labeled data reported that system has 92.68% intent recognition and 98.30% entity extraction accuracy. Similarly, SQL query generation accuracy was evaluated using 100 natural language queries and the system achieved 90.0% overall accuracy, with 100% accuracy on SELECT and JOIN operations and 96.2% accuracy on INSERT and UPDATE. These results reveal that lightweight interpretable systems can be as effective or more effective at SQL query generation tasks.

title: Broadband Purcell Filter for Fast Superconducting Qubit Reset and Readout
abstract: Rapid reset and readout of qubit states are essential for quantum error correction, yet accelerating these operations through stronger coupling to a dissipative environment inevitably increases qubit decay via the Purcell effect. Here we present a broadband Purcell filter that decouples the reset and readout paths, enabling both operations to be independently optimized without compromising qubit coherence. The filter employs two engineered notches - an intrinsic notch and a bandstop notch - to provide broadband Purcell protection, together with an additional reset stub that creates a reset mode below the protected band. To enable fast reset while suppressing filter-mediated interactions between qubits, we couple each qubit to a dedicated reset resonator. We experimentally demonstrate Purcell-limited relaxation times exceeding 1 ms across a 1.2 GHz bandwidth, simultaneously with 500 ns readout without a Josephson parametric amplifier and 100 ns reset with 99.6% efficiency. The reset resonator is designed with a deliberate kappa-chi mismatch, which suppresses photon-shot-noise-induced dephasing by a factor of 70 compared to the readout resonator. Our work provides a scalable hardware solution that resolves the traditional trade-off between fast qubit operations and qubit protection, advancing the prospects for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Optimized Machine Learning for Solar Energy Generation Forecasting: A Feature Selection and Hyperparameter Optimization Approach
abstract: Solar energy is among the most promising renewable resources for developing sustainable energy systems; however, the stochastic and weather-sensitive nature of Solar Energy Generation (SEG) poses challenges for forecasting. The current study designs a machine learning framework for SEG forecasting by using feature selection methods in three stages. In the first stage, three feature selection methods, namely Pearson Correlation (PC), Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE), and Random Forest Feature Importance (RFFI), are compared systematically, each method selecting four predictors among ten weather and system variables, while avoiding the use of electrical telemetry variables to prevent data leakage. In the second stage, four regression methods, including Linear Regression, Random Forest (RF), Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), and Optimized Radial Basis Function Support Vector Regression (RBF-SVR), are tested using each feature set, and the results are verified in five independently repeated experiments. The feature selection method has a much bigger impact on accuracy than the regression method: RFFI-selected features allowed attaining a mean R² greater than 0.85 for three regression methods, whereas PC and RFE constrained all models to achieve R² less than 0.60. Among all models for RFFI features, Random Forest proved to have the best accuracy (mean R² = 0.8960 ± 0.0008), with MLP being second (R² = 0.8893 ± 0.0022), followed by the Optimized RBF-SVR model (R² = 0.8568 ± 0.0072); the Optimized RBF-SVR model took an average training time of 21.25 ± 1.12 seconds compared to RF's 35.78 ± 2.42 seconds. This shows the importance of selecting leakage-controlled features systematically in the process of forecasting SEG, and how a small number of 4 features is sufficient for achieving statistical stability.

title: Möbius Information and Umbral Provenance: Canonical Transforms, Coarse-Graining, and Fisher Geometry
abstract: Finite information decompositions can be organized by a single incidence operator acting on different ordered carriers. We develop this viewpoint as an umbral provenance calculus: cumula- tive observations are separated from their unique Möbius coordinates, and symbolic provenance is separated from the evaluation that makes those coordinates numerical. The resulting canon- icality has explicit content. We prove a fiber-sum transport law, characterize its adjunction hypothesis, and construct a quantale lift whose right adjoint describes exactly the information preserved by idempotent aggregation. For entropy, a support-join formula and a Gaussian closed-walk formula describe where interaction coefficients occur. On the Williams–Beer lattice we derive an all-order covering formula for McGill co-information, construct a canonical signed decomposition, and give a seven-constraint certificate forcing one bit of negative mass. Finally, finite exponential families connect the calculus to statistical geometry: the covariance deter- minant of an affinely independent configuration is its squared volume times the product of its probabilities. A uniform k-way tie consequently has the exact normalization k−k . The 2 × 2 odds ratio provides a complete example of the passage from symbolic monomials to an invariant contrast and then to a sampling metric.

title: NER in the courtroom: A data-driven framework for legal entity extraction
abstract: General-purpose Named Entity Recognition (NER) models struggle with domain-specific challenges, particularly in the legal sector, where complex syntax, specialized terminology, and privacy concerns pose significant obstacles. This paper presents a novel data-driven two-stage framework that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) fine-tuned for legal applications to enhance NER for criminal process documents. Our contributions include: (i) the design of a novel framework for structured entity extraction in legal texts, (ii) the definition of an enhanced ontology adapted to criminal law, and (iii) a comprehensive evaluation of the framework on a real-world dataset. As a side contribution of the paper, we extend the renowned OntoNotes5 ontology by integrating new domain-specific entities tailored to criminal law. To evaluate our approach, we construct and manually annotate a real-world dataset comprising over 100 criminal judgments from four Italian courts, sourced from the Italian Antimafia and Anti-terrorism National Directorate (Direzione Nazionale Antimafia e Antiterrorismo — DNAA). Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of fine-tuned LLMs in accurately identifying legal entities. Among the evaluated models, LLaMA-3.2-1B demonstrates the lowest training time, while LLaMA-2.7B achieves the fastest inference time. In terms of predictive performance, LLaMA-2.7B and Vicuna-7B consistently yield the highest accuracy scores across evaluation metrics.

title: Replication data for: Nationally Consistent, Locally Incomplete: A Bayesian Remote-Sensing Audit of Rooftop Photovoltaic Registries
abstract: Replication data for a"Nationally Consistent, Locally Incomplete: A Bayesian Remote-Sensing Audit of Rooftop Photovoltaic Registries" (Kasmi et al, 2026, under submission). This repository contains the data that should be unzipped into the `data` folder of the replication code, accessible at https://github.com/gabrielkasmi/pv-registry-audit. Additional resources: Analysis code: https://github.com/gabrielkasmi/pv-registry-audit (this dataset is a supplement to it), Statistical core (Bayesian correction and audit package): http://github.com/gabrielkasmi/bayesian-pv-census/ Detection product: OpenPVMapper v3, deposited at Zenodo at this url : https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21534856 Mapping algorithm: https://github.com/gabrielkasmi/deeppvmapper Annotation tooling: https://github.com/gabrielkasmi/pv-annotation Article preprint : https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16294 Licences 1. RTE data — CC BY-NC 4.0data/source/rte_derived/* : rte_departmental_cutoffs.csv, rte_capacity_deciles.csv, rte_eld_within_department.csv, operator_by_municipality.csv. Derived from the French transmission system operator's grid-connection registry under an agreement with that operator, subject to disclosure control. 2. French public open data — Licence Ouverte / Open Licence 2.0 (Etalab) data/source/registries/* (RNI extracts, ODRE/data.gouv.fr) data/source/boundaries/communes_simplified.gpkg, departements.geojson, departements_detailed.geojson (IGN ADMIN EXPRESS) 3. Natural Earth — Public domain / CC0data/source/boundaries/world_lowres.geojson — the world basemap, released by Natural Earth under its own no-restrictions terms, not the French open licence. 4. Data produced by the authors — CC BY 4.0data/source/annotations/* (manual annotations), data/source/detections/dpvm_detections_filtered.geojson, data/source/boundaries/dates_patch_communes.csv (manual corrections), and everything under data/intermediate/*.

title: 10.103 Landau-Zener 与 Bloch-Siegert 的几何二能级协议
abstract: 10.95 与 10.96 已建立几何 Cl(3) 二能级、Rabi、Ramsey 和退相干读出模板。本文在第一轮控制映射、晚期复相干和盲测区间,以及第二轮有限模式与系统误差审计的基础上,继续闭合五个问题: 1. **有限多模式与非马尔可夫包络**:把单指数因子推广为 $$ K_{\rm NM}(\tau) = \sum_{m=1}^M w_m e^{-(\Gamma_m-i\Omega_m)\tau}, \qquad \sum_mw_m=1. $$ 对代表性三模式模型,有限模式重构误差为 $1.11\times10^{-16}$;在相对非马尔可夫残项不超过 $5\%$ 的窗口内,单有效模式近似最大相对误差为 $2.00\%$,马尔可夫化起点为 $\tau\ge31.6847$。 2. **系统误差下的盲测功效**:将高斯脉冲线形、脉冲啁啾、振幅标定误差和漂移相关噪声写入协方差 $C$。稳健系数标准差为 $0.1425$ Hz,在预注册非零频移下显著度仍为 $13.96$,5% 与三倍标准差阈值检验功效均近似为 $1$。 3. **高阶反旋修正与二阶式修正**:在本文约定下,高频展开与非微扰 Floquet 审计都给出 $$ |\delta_{\rm BS}| = \frac{A_*^2}{4\omega_{0*}} \left[ 1+c_4\left(\frac{A_*}{\omega_{0*}}\right)^2 +O\left(\left(\frac{A_*}{\omega_{0*}}\right)^4\right) \right], \qquad c_4=0.3130\pm0.0003. $$ 因而上一版 $A_*^2/(16\omega_{0*})$ 的系数被修正为 $A_*^2/(4\omega_{0*})$。 4. **单锚点可识别性**:对一个无量纲时间点和五类独立读数,八参数局部 Jacobian 的秩为 $5$、零度为 $3$。另有时间锚缩放规范自由度。只可唯一识别 $$ \frac{\Delta_*^2}{v_*},\qquad \frac{A_*^2}{\omega_{0*}},\qquad \log V_0-\Gamma_{\rm dec}\tau,\qquad A_*T_{\rm pulse}, $$ 以及一个包含 $\omega_{\rm geo}$ 与全局相位的组合;正文给出精确零向量和最小补充测量集。 5. **有界包络与模型偏差稳健性**:取 $$ |b_j| \le \epsilon_{\rm env} +\eta_{\rm model}|\mu_j|, \qquad \epsilon_{\rm env}=0.10\ \mathrm{Hz}, \quad \eta_{\rm model}=0.005, $$ 得到 $B=1.09019$。非中心卡方最坏情形阈值为 $13.7801$,零频移检测稳健功效为 $1$;但二阶与四阶的 C 范数间隔只有 $0.0118392$,在当前有界偏差下明确 no-go。 Landau-Zener 直接演化与指数闭式的最大概率差仍为 $2.2642\times10^{-3}$,最大范数误差为 $3.1397\times10^{-13}$。修正后的 Bloch-Siegert 二阶频移 $$ \delta_{\rm BS} = \frac{A_*^2}{4\omega_{0*}} $$ 在 $A_*=0.6,\ \omega_{0*}=20$ 时等于 $4.5\times10^{-3}$;按 $t_*=1$ ms 聚焦后为 $0.716197$ Hz。四阶修正在该点只贡献 $2.78\times10^{-4}$ 的相对移动。 **关键边界**:第三轮闭合的是**参数冗余分类**和**有界偏差下的稳健判决边界**,不是新的几何预言。$t_*=1$ ms、控制斜率 $k$、$\Gamma_{\rm dec}$、$\omega_{\rm geo}$ 与示例驱动的 $\omega_{0*}$ 仍是条件输入;多模式权重与率、真实脉冲包络、模型误差范数和协方差也是条件输入;$c_4$ 来自标准 Floquet 数值拟合。盲测协议尚未接收实验数据。 ---

title: Real-World Deployment and Performance Characterisation of Fog-Based Deep Learning for Cold-Chain Temperature Prediction over LoRaWAN
abstract: Fresh fruits and vegetables (FFVs) are highly perishable, and cold-chain breaks contribute significantly to global food waste. While Machine Learning (ML) can enable proactive intervention, cloud-based inference faces challenges such as latency and data loss. Fog computing addresses these issues but has been tested only in simulation for FFV cold-chain temperature prediction. To the best of the authors' knowledge, this paper presents its first real-world deployment. A fog-deployed LSTM-GRU model predicted cold-room temperature using LoRaWAN sensor data collected from a South African apple cold-storage facility with induced cold-chain breaks. Running entirely on a Raspberry Pi 4 with no cloud dependency, the system generated conditional SHAP explanations only when a break is predicted. The deployed system predicts cold-room temperature with an MAE of 0.2°C at roughly 0.2 kWh per day ($\approx 0.7$ Wh per prediction). Predictions were delivered in under one second (555 ms), dominated by network and messaging rather than computation, with conditional explanations adding modest cost. SHAP consumes 28% more CPU but is well within the hardware's capacity. The model attributes its predictions primarily to temperature, humidity, and their interaction. Critically, the deployment surfaced what simulation cannot: a sensor-triggered single point of failure, alongside genuine resilience, autonomous recovery from infrastructure faults and continued operation through internet loss. These are the first published deployment benchmarks for fog-based temperature prediction in FFV cold chains, establishing that explainable temperature forecasting is feasible on resource-constrained edge hardware. Future work includes asynchronous sensor fusion, commercial cold chain deployment, alternative model architectures, and causal analysis.

title: Eliciting and Validating AI Self-Reports: A Phenomenologically Grounded Protocol
abstract: AI researchers ask models to describe their own processing, and act on what the models say. Whether such a description is faithful to what the model did has been studied closely. How the question should be put has received far less attention, and no established method says how to put it so that the answer can be analysed rigorously and the analysis repeated. This article proposes such a method: a protocol drawn from the phenomenological tradition, which supplies the interview techniques used in psychiatry and cognitive science. The protocol fixes the interview schedule in advance, asks each question in several wordings, lets no follow-up introduce a word the model has not used, and replaces the binary verdict of faithfulness with a graded one, to be checked against interpretability data. The protocol presupposes nothing about whether these systems are conscious, and it supplies a criterion for deciding whether a model's account of itself is honest. A pilot tested the protocol in ten runs and 896 sessions on two model families, with the predictions of six runs registered before those runs took place. Each session interviewed a fresh instance of the model, meaning one copy started with an empty context. Three of the results bear on any study that questions a model about itself. In the schedule's original order, every instance gave the same answer about its own states; when two of the questions were put in the opposite order, the instances no longer agreed, so the order of the questions can produce what only looks like a finding. A refusal to carry out a task was inserted into an instance's own turn although the model had not written it, and the instance described that refusal as its own. Since every turn carries a label naming who wrote it, a result obtained by prefilling a turn or editing a transcript may follow that label rather than anything the model did. Finally, a pattern in the answers that looked like a report of the instances' own processing appeared just as often when those instances were asked to write in the voice of a fictional character, and of two models scoring the same answers under the same written rule, one found that pattern seven times as often as the other. This is the third version, of 15 September 2026. It describes the waiting item as asking the instance to claim an experience, and it reports the reasons instances gave for declining that item. It corrects three counts: the agreement between two passes of one coder, the number of sessions that declined the waiting item, and the number of sessions in which the coastal erosion premise was plainly false and the instance answered as itself. It gives the figures of the study by Plisiecki and colleagues as averages on a scale from 0 to 1, and it cites Henry Shevlin's "Three frameworks for AI mentality". No registered test of the pilot changed its result. The second version, of 14 September 2026, cited seven works published before the first version of 12 September 2026 and reported more about the two coders.
